title: solution.tex Lemma bound: missing justification that b_2 lies on D and f(b_2)=(0,-l(f(B)))

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** solution.tex, proof of Lemma \ref{lem:bound}, the $D$-estimate.

The unfolding estimate begins 'the point $f(b_2)=(0,y)$ with $y\le0$ splits $f(D)$ into two subarcs $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$.' Two facts are used but not proved:

1. **$b_2\in D$ (so that $f(b_2)$ genuinely lies on the curve $f(D)$ and splits it).** $b_2$ is the bottom endpoint of the crosscut $B$, lying on the bottom boundary. $D$ is the bottom boundary segment joining the bottom endpoints of $A$ and $G(A)$. One must invoke admissibility $A\prec B\prec G(A)$, i.e. $m(A)<m(B)<m(A)+\beta$, to conclude the $x$-coordinate of $b_2$ lies strictly between the bottom endpoints of $A$ and $G(A)$, hence $b_2\in D$ and $f(b_2)\in f(D)$. Without this, splitting $f(D)$ at $f(b_2)$ is unjustified.

2. **$f(b_2)=(0,-\ell(f(B)))$, so $|y|=\ell(f(B))$.** The normalization places $f(B)$ on the non-positive $Y$-axis with top endpoint at the origin. Since $b_2$ is the bottom endpoint of $B$, $f(b_2)$ is the bottom endpoint of $f(B)$, i.e. $(0,-\ell(f(B)))$, giving the equality $|y|=\ell(f(B))>1$, hence $|2y|>2$. The text writes $|2y|\ge2\ell(f(B))$ without deriving where $y$ comes from.

Partially overlaps prob-02-5 (items 3-4); the specific membership step $b_2\in D$ via admissibility is a distinct missing link.
